According to recent reports, hier, lors de sa conférence de presse, Ian Cathro a donné de bonnes nouvelles de notre gardien : "Ca suit son cours positivement pour Gautier Larsonneur. Un retour en décembre n’est pas impossible, mais je ne peux pas être plus précis que ça.".

Recent findings suggest that la Pravda du jour fait ce matin le portrait du meilleur buteur de Ligue 2, le jeune rémois Yaya Fofana. Déja sur les tablettes de Stuttgart, Trabzonspor et Galatasaray, il sera un des joueurs à museler pour les Verts demain soir :.

Avec 10 buts en 12 matchs cette saison (sur 18 frappes cadrées), plus 2 passes décisives, le milieu rémois (22 ans) est la révélation de cette phase aller. « Il pourrait frapper de cinquante mètres, il marquerait, en ce moment » sourit un scout bluffé par l’efficacité de l’Ivoirien, tout juste appelé chez les Eléphants (sans jouer) (…) Selon Mathieu Lacour, le directeur sportif de Reims, « ce qu’il fait aujourd’hui, il l’a fait pendant trois mois en L1 déjà (à l’entame de la saison 2024-2025). C’est un talent exceptionnel, avec une qualité technique au-dessus de la moyenne, il fait 12km par match, il a les meilleures datas physiques de l’effectif. C’est sans doute notre plus grand talent depuis Hugo Ekitike. » Parmi les observateurs, la question est de mesurer à quel point la séquence actuelle représente fidèlement son niveau. « Oui, ça l’est. Il a un sens du but et du déplacement assez épatant. C’est un garçon déjà assez complet, capable de jouer dans plein de positions différentes. Il a un vrai profil. » analyse Hervé Renard, son sélectionneur (…) Reims n’entend pas perdre son talent cet hiver. A moins qu’un club ne formule une offre avec un prêt immédiat dans l’effectif champenois. « Il ne vaut pas moins que Patrick Zabi vendu 25M€ au Paris FC l’été dernier) » estime-t-on au club (…) « Il faudra qu’il passe par une étape avant d’aller plus haut. Il lui faut du temps de jeu pour se développer encore », juge Renard.

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • In a recent development, getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • Industry observers note that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

In a recent development, getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

Industry observers note that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

Recent findings suggest that you might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

According to recent reports, an obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it notable to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

Sources indicate that as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

Industry observers note that favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

It has been revealed that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier remarked than done, though.

Sources indicate that whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop remarked the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

#84572. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

📅 16 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5987 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5987 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
  • Recent findings suggest that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
  • In a recent development, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the fresh signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

Recent findings suggest that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

In a recent development, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Recent findings suggest that title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

According to recent reports, first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

It has been revealed that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

Sources indicate that “They are really good examples,” Arteta stated. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

It has been revealed that here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

Industry observers note that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

City, in contrast to their opponents, indicated a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where fresh boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Recent findings suggest that throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer aims remain up in the air for both camps.

According to recent reports, city appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

In a recent development, arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

Quatre jeunes buteurs au profil intéressant… mais différent de celui de Romelu Lukaku dont la puissance pouvait faire valser dans le décor n’importe quel défenseur une fois lancé vers le but. Cet été, repéré par le Club Bruges, Jeoffrey Mbambi a paraphé son premier contrat pro en Venise du Nord, le liant aux Blauw & Zwart jusqu’en 2029.

Dans le noyau des U18, l’adaptation s’est bien déroulée puisque le Brabançon a disputé 8 rencontres et planté 7 buts. Des débuts plus que prometteurs à 15 ans, faut-il encore le rappeler, qui lui permettent de s’entraîner de temps à autre avec le Club NXT, les U23 évoluant en Challenger Pro League. Jeoffrey Mbambi ne devrait pas tarder avant de faire ses débuts dans le football professionnel belge. Certaines rumeurs l’envoient déjà dans les plus grands clubs européens à l’affût.".

Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dutchnews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND noted the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB introduced an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser noted it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

Recent findings suggest that “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players noted they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

According to recent reports, “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that indicates I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

Les dirigeants du club corse ont pris leur temps mais, surtout, ont voulu se donner le maximum de réflexion. Plusieurs noms ont circulé avant l'officialisation du nouveau coach qui sera Ghislain Printant, ainsi que l'indique Corse-Matin. Le SEC Bastia n'a pas tardé a apporter la confirmation. Dans le même communiqué, le club indique, tout en le remerciant, que Michel Moretti reste à son poste d'adjoint.

In a recent development, "L'arrivée de Ghislain Printant ne doit donc rien à l'improvisation, encore moins à la précipitation. Le coach qui a fait monter le Sporting à Paris pour la finale de la Coupe de la Ligue, en avril 2015, a toujours clamé son amour du club, y compris lorsqu'il a été démis de ses fonctions en janvier 2016 au profit de son adjoint d'alors, François Ciccolini.Loyal, certes, mais aussi compétent puisqu'au-delà de ses premières fonctions de formateur, il a longtemps été un entraîneur adjoint, à Montpellier, bien sûr, mais aussi à Marseille, à Saint-Etienne, avec la sélection de Côte d'Ivoire, toujours avec son ami de longue date, le regretté Jean-Louis Gasset.".

In a recent development, le quotidien précise : "Certes, le club a changé depuis son passage entre 2010 et 2016, époque durant laquelle il a connu Gilles Cioni, l'actuel coordinateur sportif du Sporting. Pour autant, lors d'un récent entretien avec notre titre, il avait démontré qu'il suivait toujours l'actualité du club, d'autant que son fils, Florian, y était entraîneur des gardiens avant de s'engager avec Evian-Thonon. Le nouveau coach du Sporting devrait bien évidemment être dans les travées d'Armand-Cesari pour le match face à Villefranche, ce samedi 21 novembre. Lundi il devrait diriger sa première séance et tenir une conférence de presse de présentation.".

Ghislain Printant était arrivé à l'ASSE en décembre 2017, comme adjoint de  Jean-Louis Gasset. Le duo succédait à Oscar Garcia, Julien Sablé ayant assuré un interim de 35 jours. Après une belle fin de saison 2017-2018, et une non moins belle saison 2018-2019, ponctuée par une 4ème place qualificative pour l'Europa League, il a été nommé entraîneur principal de l'ASSE, le 6 juin 2019, suite au départ de Jean-Louis Gasset. Mais le début de saison 2019-2020 est mitigé et son contrat sera résilié le 4 octobre 2019, laissant la place à Claude Puel.

Quelques mois plus tard, le 10 août 2020, Ghislain Printant va rejoindre son ami Jean-Louis Gasset et devenir son adjoint aux Girondins de Bordeaux.

Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • According to recent reports, is football a moral force for good?
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

According to recent reports, is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

In a recent development, football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

Industry observers note that in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

It has been revealed that if humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

Recent findings suggest that to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Industry observers note that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

It has been revealed that football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

In a recent development, as metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

Industry observers note that the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

Industry observers note that in a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

It has been revealed that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise notable questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

According to recent reports, van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

Sources indicate that “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4322 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the upcoming Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions.
  • “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City.
  • There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the upcoming Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

Recent findings suggest that “They know how to do it,” Arteta noted of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

Sources indicate that “Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they demonstrated it,” Lampard remarked. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard stated Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

According to recent reports, before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

Sources indicate that if that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

Sources indicate that the energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Industry observers note that coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

In a recent development, saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the newly introduced £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

Sources indicate that odegaard demonstrated in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

It has been revealed that "It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx.

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

Recent findings suggest that "How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I.

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE.

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the newly introduced season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J.

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Sources indicate that coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

It has been revealed that lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Recent findings suggest that lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

It has been revealed that tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

It has been revealed that the visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

It has been revealed that the ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a major deflection and flies out for a corner.

According to recent reports, from a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

Recent findings suggest that white overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6.

In a recent development, odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/.

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

According to recent reports, tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

It has been revealed that at the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Industry observers note that christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

In a recent development, arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

In a recent development, coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

In a recent development, van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

Industry observers note that the German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

In a recent development, arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

According to recent reports, tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Sources indicate that following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

Newly introduced Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The fresh signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss mentioned: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”.

In a recent development, another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so vital to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Industry observers note that odegaard comes into the fresh Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta indicates Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T.

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W.

According to recent reports, on Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a fresh chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he remarked.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”.

It has been revealed that arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

It has been revealed that riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

Recent findings suggest that the Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

According to recent reports, "I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w.

Upcoming signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF.

Recent findings suggest that as Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA.

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”.

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy.

It has been revealed that good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a fresh season. A classic Arteta-ism.

It has been revealed that the assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without upcoming £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has noted he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta stated. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”.

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”.

In a recent development, this is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

💡 Key Takeaways

Sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en juin 2029 mais prêté cette saison au FC Séville (avec une option d'achat estimée à 25 M€), Lucas Stassin s'est brièvement confié à DAZN avant le derby contre le Betis programmé ce samedi à 18h30.

Industry observers note that "On est 6e de Liga, je trouve que c'est un bon début de saison. Maintenant, on peut toujours faire mieux. Quand on regarde les matches où on a perdu des points, ça se joue toujours à des petits détails. Il faut voir le positif, on est dans le top 6 et on va essayer de rester dedans toute la saison. Franchement on m'a très bien accueilli. Le team manager ici est très, très cool. Il parle français en plus. je me suis très vite adapté au groupe. Il y a d'autres francophones dans le groupe [notamment Arouna Sangante, Lucien Agoumé et Youssouf Fofana, ndp2], on parle du championnat de France, forcément. On peut parler français entre nous, c'est cool de parler la langue maternelle. On parle des clubs par où on est passé et des joueurs contre qui on a joué.

Sources indicate that je garde un très, très bon souvenir de Saint-Etienne parce que j'y ai quand même passé une belle saison en Ligue 1 avec un bon derby forcément. Je garde un très bon souvenir de mes coéquipiers et du staff même s'ils ont changé beaucoup de staff. En Espagne, il y-a forcément les trois grosses équipes [Barça, Real, Atletico, ndp2] alors qu'en France il y a moins ça, chaque année est un peu différente. En Espagne les duels sont quand même un peu plus intensifs. La mentalité est différente sur le terrain, c'est vraiment toujours à 200% du début jusqu'à la fin du match. Techniquement, il y a énormément de bons joueurs en Liga même si en France il y avait déjà énormément de qualités, ça m'avait impressionné quand j'étais arrivé.

It has been revealed that le derby sévillan, on m'en a parlé depuis que je suis là. On en parle beaucoup. On sait que c'est un très, très gros derby. Avec Lyon et Saint-Etienne, je sais forcément l'ambiance qu'il pourrait y avoir, l'enthousiasme, donc j'ai vraiment hâte de voir comment va être l'ambiance ici. On veut surtout essayer de gagner ce derby pour passer une bonne soirée et une bonne semaine. On se prépare beaucoup, on parle beaucoup de ça à l'entraînement. On va aborder ce match avec une bonne envie. Si le fait de pouvoir me distinguer lors du derby peut être important et intéressant dans la perspective d'être rappelé chez les Diables Rouges ? Ouais, forcément, on a toujours l'objectif de performer en club pour être repris en équipe nationale. La prochaine sélection est en mars, je vais tout faire d'ici-là pour essayer d'avoir des chances d'être repris.".

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Industry observers note that team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:48 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:41 EST, 17 November 2026.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but indicates he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he said on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment.

He remarked without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old.

The Man United legend mentioned he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career.

Sources indicate that 'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'.

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

Recent findings suggest that 'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney mentioned. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

It has been revealed that 'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'.

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

According to recent reports, 'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight.

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

It has been revealed that 'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

Industry observers note that 'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'.

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

He previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'.

Industry observers note that he added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

Sources indicate that 'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'.

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show.

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle.

He also mentioned part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

Recent findings suggest that in his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'.

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career.

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney stated: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

Expulsé contre les Verts en mars 2017 lors d'un match nul et vierge à Furiani pour avoir mis un coup de pied au visage de Vincent Pajot, Nicolas Saint-Ruf a marqué hier à l'occasion de son premier match de la saison de L2 l'unique but de la victoire de son équipe contre Dijon.

Revenu provisoirement à hauteur des leaders stéphanois, le défenseur guadeloupéen de 34 ans se réjouit du prochain déplacement de l'ASNL à Saint-Etienne (le samedi 5 décembre à 20h00), comme l'a relayé la Pravda au sortir de son succès contre le DFCO.

"J'ai un rôle vital parce qu'on a un groupe qui est jeune. C'est important pour moi de montrer l'exemple. C'est kiffant ce soir, mais ça va l'être encore plus dans le Chaudron dans deux semaines.".
